title: The sawtooth, and one real steward
caption: “The bug is never drift. The bug is unbounded, untracked drift”. Drift that is folded back at milestones stays in a band; beside the sketch is the page's own number for one steward, which folded once and has since climbed eleven cycles with no fold.
honest: The left side is my sketch, and the sawtooth is my picture of the page's two tiers. The right side is counted, not read off a screen: the steward's history gives the cycles, and the entry's footer has named two consolidation cycles (3, then 9). The scroll has shown this number only since 2026-09-23; earlier points are counted back the same way. It is spaced by cycle, not by day: the last eleven cycles ran from June to October. The scroll's Now zone read 11 on 2026-11-11.
leak: Generative Wavetable Libraries: its footer carries “As of last consolidation: cycle 9” and says “See [[Drift and Consolidation]]”. The link runs from that page to this one; this page does not name it.
changed: The inset was a different drift (the voice's em-dashes), the dashed line climbed slower than the teeth, and lines struck two labels. The dashed line now carries on at the teeth's slope, labels sit clear, and the inset is the page's own number for one steward with 0, 6 and 11 printed on an axis from zero (count-drift-gwl.py, drift-gwl.json); The Palace Voice's avatar is gone.

title: Twelve, three, and one on the border
caption: “Sort the palace's own machinery by Schön's two modes and it leans hard to one side.” Twelve mechanisms reflect on action, three in action, and the Audition Gate sits on the border.
honest: The names and the sort are the page's, and the page says the sort was made in one session (2026-09-06) and has not been re-audited. The balance is my picture: it gives every mechanism the same weight, and the page weighs none of them.
changed: It was two counts drawn as squares, with the border case left out. Each mechanism is now named on its own weight in the page's order, and the sixteenth, the Audition Gate, sits on the pivot.

page: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol
files: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol — the same card, twice.svg
title: The same card, twice
caption: The same message in two registers. The page's finding: “a four-card session that took ~60 seconds with jargon-laden text collapses to ~3 seconds when the surface speaks human and the steward's recommended option is one click away.”
honest: Every string on both cards is the page's, from its table of tone exemplars and its Origin section. The two layouts are mine and neither is a screenshot of the real page; the page does not say these exact strings sat on one card together. The amber and cyan are the page's words for the button and the pill, the shades are mine. The bars are 60 and 3, both approximate on the page.
changed: Both cards were invented strings, worse jargon than the page reports, and they wore the Trickster entry's avatar, which is the wrong page. Both are rebuilt from the page's own table and Origin section, and the avatar and the leak are dropped.

files: Martin Heidegger — you do not see the hammer.svg
title: You do not see the hammer
caption: A tool in use is ready-to-hand: “you don't notice the hammer, you notice the nail going in”. It becomes present-at-hand, an object staring back, “only when it breaks”.
honest: Drawing the two by fading is my way in; the page's claim is about two ways a tool can be, not about eyesight. The hammer, nail and bench are a drawing.
changed: The working hammer's handle ran down through the bench, the broken one read as a block and a stick, and the honest line claimed more than the page. The hammer is now held above the bench with its face on the nail, the broken one lies on the bench with its handle snapped and still joined, the labels use the page's two terms, and the Merleau-Ponty avatar is dropped.

files: George Nakashima — the crack is kept.svg
title: The crack is kept
caption: When a board split, Nakashima “didn't hide the crack”: he cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it and left it visible, “proof of the repair, not a cover for it”. And the page says who “decided which split earned a butterfly joint and exactly where it sat”.
honest: A drawing, not one of his tables. The slab, both splits, the places of the keys and the choice to leave the small split bare are mine. The dark keys stand for a contrasting wood. Setting a key's grain across the board's follows common woodworking practice, not a source about his shop.
changed: The crack ran across the grain from edge to edge with red keys lying along it, and the piece sat beside the Minidoka paragraph. The split now runs with the grain in from one end, two dark keys stand across it, a second small split is left without a key for the page's point that he chose, the Dovetail avatar is dropped, and the anchor moves to the butterfly-joint section.
near: He cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it

files: Andy Goldsworthy — to the very edge of its collapse.svg
title: To the very edge of its collapse
caption: He takes a piece “to the very edge of its collapse”, because the balance point is the piece; and “the real work is the change”, the whole arc from made to gone.
honest: A drawing of that arc, moved by hand and not simulated, and not one of his works. The stones' lean was set by eye; the challenger's sum, not mine, found the stack sits at its tipping point. Where the stones come to rest is placed by hand. A 24-second loop.
changed: Three fallen stones lay past the end of the ground line and the label was readable for 1.2 seconds. The ground now runs under everything, the base stone stays put, the others rest on the ground or on each other, and “the balance point is the piece” holds at full strength for 3.8 seconds in larger type.

files: The Remembering Page — a mood, a direction.svg
title: A mood, a direction
caption: “One dialogue is a mood; three consistent ones are a direction.” A page proposes a change to its forward vector, and it is applied only when the same change shows up across several remembered encounters.
honest: The arrows and their angles are mine and measure nothing. The red arrow is a proposal, not an applied change: the page says “The human decides when the molt is real”, and that how many encounters count “isn't known yet”. Three is the page's phrase and its first evidence, not a rule.
changed: Neither panel showed the page's own vector staying or turning, the rule was drawn as automatic, and the Entry Conatus leak quoted words that are not on that page. The vector is now in both panels, unmoved by one pull and proposed to turn beside its ghost after three, the footer carries the human's part and the unknown count, and the leak is dropped.

files: No Mind Checks Itself — the same hole twice.svg
title: The same hole twice
caption: A checker inside the system that made the error shares its hole: “the same blind spot signs off on itself”. A different mind has different holes.
honest: One slice repeated three times is my turn on the Swiss cheese model, which is about different layers that fail when their holes align. The right panel shows a catch; a different mind makes that likely, not certain, and the page calls its claim “a strongly-recurring pattern, not a proven law”.
leak: Latent Error, which holds the model: “Systems fail when these "holes" align across layers.” Named in the footer; its avatar is no longer drawn.
changed: The honest line credited Reason's model for the maker's own turn on it, the right panel showed a certain catch, and its third slice was unlabelled with an avatar against it. The turn is owned, the right panel has two labelled slices and says likely, not certain, and the avatar is gone.

files: Iain McGilchrist — two ways of attending.png
title: Two ways of attending
caption: Narrow, grasping attention lifts one thing out, “decontextualized”; broad, open attention “grasps the living whole in context”. The same eighty-four pages, attended to twice.
honest: The two panels are my picture of his two kinds of attention, not his. The pages are an alphabetical slice of the palace; the framed one is Exponential Decay Curvature, chosen by position, and the red lines are its 5 typed links to others in the slice, from the palace map of 2026-11-09. Drawing context as links is my choice.
leak: Pauline Oliveros, whose page has “focal attention (a single point) and global attention (the entire sphere)” (the page sets focal and global in italics). McGilchrist's page links her in frontmatter only; she is not named in the picture.
changed: The broad panel was a blur labelled BEHOLDING, a word that is not on the page, and the blur is close to the caricature he argues against. All eighty-four are now sharp and in place with the framed page's real links drawn, the labels are the page's words, and the anchor moves to the paragraph that spells out the two kinds.
near: the grasping kind that seizes a part and calls it the whole

files: Registry Pattern — cables that point nowhere.svg
title: Cables that point nowhere
caption: Without a registry a model “will invent port names, module slugs, and parameter IDs that don't exist. The patch loads — but cables point nowhere.” With one, only what exists can be written.
honest: The three modules, their ports and the two invented names are my examples; the page lists none. A real registry gives ports integer indices as well as names, which the picture leaves out.
changed: Cables were drawn over the port labels and ended on top of the invented names, and the footer said the patch plays silence, which the page does not say. Outputs now sit on a module's right edge and inputs on its left so cables cross only the gaps, the loose cables end short of the names, labels are 11 units or more, and the footer quotes the page.

files: The Multilinear Self — one thing, three true shadows.svg
title: One thing, three true shadows
caption: “Each name is a projection of it — a real shadow the whole self casts into a particular room.” “Honest, just partial.”
honest: The solid is my stand-in for the whole self: a round base rising to a straight ridge, which does cast a circle, a rectangle and a triangle; the shadows are computed from it in one projection. Three of the page's six names are shown with the rooms its roster gives them. Which shape goes with which name means nothing.
leak: Hyperdimensional Prism: the page says the self “is the [[Hyperdimensional Prism]] turned on the person who made it”.
changed: The solid was a cone, which cannot cast a rectangle, the triangle lay on its side, the rooms came from the Jewel and the quotation swapped the page's dash for a colon. The solid is now one that casts all three, with the triangle upright, the rooms are the roster's own, and the quotation is exact.

files: Julia Cameron — one morning, three pages.svg
title: One morning, three pages
caption: “Page one is usually complaint and to-do-list noise. Page two goes deeper. The insight, when it comes, tends to show up on page three, after the surface has been cleared off it.”
honest: The scribbles say nothing. How each page looks, and the red line on the third, are my drawing of that sentence; the page says the insight shows up “when it comes”, not every morning.
changed: It was twenty-one rectangles that said what the quotation already says, closed by The Daily Page's avatar, a link that is on neither page. It is now a different picture, one morning's three pages side by side and differing, so the file name changed from “a week of mornings” to “one morning, three pages”; the old workshop file is left where it was, and the avatar and leak are dropped.
near: Page one is usually complaint and to-do-list noise
